name: Shipped reference
note: The vowels are averages from published studies of other people's voices; the pitch bands are a practical reference, not a published norm. None of it is a target: where a band sits is a fact, which of them is a goal is between you and your clinician. Replace any of it in Settings.

sources.pitch_bands: Typical male and female speaking ranges as drawn by the voice-training apps in common clinical use. Not taken from a paper: a practical reference for placing a reading at a glance, not a published norm. Set your own in Settings.
sources.en: Hillenbrand, J. M., Getty, L. A., Clark, M. J. and Wheeler, K. (1995), Acoustic characteristics of American English vowels, JASA 97, 3099-3111. Means over the steady-state measurements in the study's published data file, 45 men and 48 women, h-V-d words read in isolation. A token whose formant the study marks unmeasurable is left out of its own average.
sources.pt: Escudero, P., Boersma, P., Rauber, A. S. and Bion, R. A. H. (2009), A cross-dialect acoustic description of vowels: Brazilian and European Portuguese, JASA 126, 1379-1393, Table I, Brazilian Portuguese. Geometric averages over ten women and ten men, one stressed vowel inside a nonce word in a carrier sentence.
